- Overestimate prices after recent spikes; model tends to overshoot upward momentum.
- Underestimate downward corrections after negative sentiment; model fails to fully absorb bearish signals.
- When sentiment is strongly negative (e.g., < -0.30), reduce forecasted price by 5–10% relative to prior peak.
- When sentiment is strongly positive (e.g., > 0.30), slightly increase forecasted price but cap at 10% above recent high.
- Model exhibits mean reversion bias: overreacts to short-term volatility, underestimates long-term trend persistence.
- Forecast horizon 30d often lags true price by 1–3 days; adjust for 1–2 day lag in price movement.
- If sentiment turns sharply negative after a spike, model fails to anticipate sharp reversal — apply downward correction of 5–15%.
- Avoid overfitting to recent highs; if last 3–5 days show strong upward momentum, reduce forecast slope to avoid overcorrection.
